concept_summary: A full-service restaurant with full kitchen, beer and wine service (ABC Type 41), approximately 50 seats and 5 employees, tenant improvements and exterior signage, at 2183 Mission St in the Mission Street NCT zoning district.

overall.line: Of the 4 approvals this concept needs: 2 further review (zoning and use, building permit and change of use), 1 insufficient information (alcohol licence), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Obtain written confirmation from SF Planning that the district-wide cap of 167 eating and drinking uses is not exceeded, then file a Conditional Use Authorization application under Planning Code § 303 for the Restaurant use.

lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Restaurant (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 754, in force since before 2022-01-01).

findings.text: The Building Code classifies a restaurant or bar as Assembly Group A-2 if the occupant load is 50 or more, or Group B if fewer than 50; the description does not state whether the occupant load is above or below 50, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.

The existing occupancy group of the space is not shown in public records; only an architect's review of plans or an inspection can establish the current occupancy, so whether a change of occupancy is required is not established.

Building permit fees are a percentage of construction valuation; for a restaurant kitchen build-out with hood, finishes and ADA upgrades, expect $800–$15,000 depending on scope, plus separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits pulled by licensed subcontractors.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full conditional use authorization to legalize a restaurant (Bissap Baobab) at 3372 19th St (192 m, NCT-MISSION zoning) that filed Sept 2018 and was approved March 2019 with 14 conditions. This is a use-decision hearing, the type 2183 Mission would face.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The only recent CUA for a restaurant in NCT-MISSION within 1,000 ft was approved with conditions but took six months from filing to approval. Key conditions included hours limited to Tues–Sun 11 a.m.–1:45 a.m., soundproofing, odor control, sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, and a community liaison requirement. Extended late-night hours (until 1:45 a.m.) were permitted.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to establish a new restaurant in a vacant commercial space at 600 South Van Ness (191 m, UMU zoning, Mission area), filed March 2018, approved Aug 2018 (5.5 months). This represents a change-of-use approval in the Mission neighborhood subject to Mission 2016 Interim Zoning Controls.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Change-of-use CUA for a new restaurant in the Mission area was approved without extracted conditions within 5.5 months. UMU zoning treated restaurants more favorably than NCT-MISSION, but the case shows Planning approved new restaurant concepts during the Mission Interim Controls period.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for a continuation restaurant use at 3382 18th St (18 m away, NCT-MISSION zoning, essentially next door), approved Jan 2021 citing Planning Code §§ 754 and 249.60. This is the closest comparable geographically.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a restaurant continuation at the property immediately adjacent (18 m) under § 754 (NCT-MISSION restaurant rules) and § 249.60 (Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules). Agency referrals for continuations are routinely approved; a change of use triggers a conditional use hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral approving a Limited Restaurant (Ramenwell) at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) as an existing permitted use under § 754 and the Mission Alcohol SUD rules (§§ 781.8 and 249.60), approved Aug 2018.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a limited restaurant very close by (31 m) within the Mission Alcohol SUD, citing both the NCT-MISSION district rules (§ 754) and the Special Use District overlay (§§ 781.8, 249.60). Limited restaurants face fewer hurdles than full restaurants, but the case confirms the dual-layer review within the SUD.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 ABC referral at 3378 18th St (31 m, NCT-MISSION) for a continuation of an existing restaurant use, approved April 2018. Same concept (restaurant with beer/wine) at nearly the same location.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 41 license for a restaurant continuation 31 m away as an agency referral in three weeks. Continuations are fast-tracked; a new restaurant filing as a change of use will face the full conditional use process with a Commission hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 47 (full-liquor) ABC referral for a restaurant at 2293 Mission St (186 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Sept 2020 as a continuation under § 754. Illustrates how alcohol licenses are handled within the district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 47 full-bar license for an existing restaurant 186 m away under § 754 as an agency referral. Full-liquor licenses are permitted for restaurants in the Mission Alcohol SUD if the restaurant operates as a Bona Fide Eating Place; the concept's Type 41 is less restrictive.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health department referral for a full-service restaurant at 2152 Mission St (63 m, NCT-MISSION), approved Nov 2018 (filed April 2017) as a continuation under §§ 790.92 and 712.42. This referral took 19 months, unusually long for an agency matter.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A restaurant continuation 63 m away was approved but took 19 months from filing to approval—an outlier timeline for an agency referral, suggesting administrative delays or incomplete submissions. Highlights the importance of complete plan sets and proactive coordination with all referral departments.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with SF Planning in writing that the district-wide cap of 167 eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION is not exceeded.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email or call a Planning Department zoning planner and request written confirmation of the current count of Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars in the NCT-MISSION zoning district against the cap of 167 in Planning Code § 754 Table 754 Note 7. Ask whether a new restaurant at 2183 Mission St would be permitted under the cap. Request a Letter of Determination or email confirmation before filing the CUA application, because the cap is a threshold question that can make the use not permitted.

filing_playbook.action: File DPH plan check for the new restaurant kitchen and finishes while the CUA is pending.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The plan check fee is $2,207 (8 hours at $276/hour for a new restaurant, FY 2026–27). Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% construction complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance, both with your assigned plan reviewer.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost are for the entitlement path approvals when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization, Health Permit to Operate, and Building Permit with change of use. The 120–300 day range is the time to approval and reflects the CUA as the critical path (5–7 months filing to hearing, typically approved 2–4 weeks after the hearing once the motion is drafted), plus overlapping plan check and building permit review. The building permit is issued after the CUA is approved, and DPH issues the health permit after the final inspection passes. Construction time is not included. The $6,800–$23,000 cost range includes the CUA filing fee (~$3,150), DPH plan check ($2,207), DPH permit to operate ($470), building permit fees ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation), Fire place-of-assembly permit if occupant load ≥ 50 ($446–$1,500), and FOG interceptor registration ($0–$500). It does not include construction costs, the ABC Type 41 licence ($1,000–$1,600, state agency, not on the entitlement path because how the licence will be obtained is not known), state and federal registrations ($70–$150 entity formation, $0 EIN and seller's permit), business registration ($55–$700), sign permit ($300–$1,500), music licences (~$600–$5,000/year combined), or professional fees (architect, contractor, expediter). The CUA fee may qualify for a First Year Free waiver if this is a new storefront business in a Priority Equity Geography; confirm eligibility with Planning. ABC review runs in parallel but is not included in the city entitlement path because the alcohol row status is insufficient information.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); Health permit to operate; Building permit with change of use

records_summary: 2183 Mission St sits in the Mission Street NCT zoning district and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The pathway analysis shows that a Restaurant here is a conditional use, and this is a change of use since the site history shows the space was most recently operated as a fast-food restaurant (legal nonconforming use, last approved 2010). The block is extremely dense: 26 food & drink businesses within 500 ft, 5 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, and 48 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft. Planning records show only 6 dated use decisions in the NCT-MISSION district within 1,000 ft over the last 5 years (1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 2 withdrawn), far too few to calculate an approval rate, but all four approvals involved restaurants or eating places.
